The Third and Fourth Derivatives of a Truncated Family's Expected Information

Source: R/d34e_truncated.R
trunc_d34expected.Rd

Computes the derivatives of order k (3 or 4) of the expected Hessian of a truncated() family on the parameter scale, as expectations under the truncated law taken by expectation().

Usage

trunc_d34expected(d, y, th, k, t = 1L)

Arguments

d

A truncated family, from truncated().

y

The response, read for its length.

th

The parameters.

k

The order, 3L or 4L.

t

Unused; it is the thread count of the registration.

Value

A list of components keyed as d3expected_names() or d4expected_names(), each of length length(y).

Details

With \(\ell = \ell_P - \log Z\) the truncated log-likelihood and \(E_{ab} = -E[\ell_a\ell_b]\), the component for a multiset \(S\) is minus the expectation of the polynomial of d34e_plan(), which reads the derivatives of \(\ell\) to order \(k + 1\). The truncation points do not depend on the parameters, so there is no boundary term. Those of \(\ell\) are the parent's less those of \(\log Z\), computed once per parameter combination by trunc_logz_derivs() and passed to the integrand. The derivatives of \(\log Z\) to order four are read from the parent's distribution function where has_exact_cdf_deriv() holds, and the parent's distribution function has no derivatives of order five, so each ratio \(d^B Z/Z\) of that order is the expectation, under the truncated law, of the complete Bell polynomial of the parent's log-density derivatives (a quadrature or a sum), which is accurate but not a closed form. Order five enters the fourth derivative only. The form \(E[\ell_{ab}]\) would need the sixth derivative of the parent.

See also

trunc_dexpected()
